design: One module, ocor-runtime/tests/conformance/fgm/test_fgm_01_10.py (the only expected_file_area), with exactly one positive and one negative qualifying case per FGM-01..FGM-10; the CAMPAIGN table quotes the scenario and oracle of each LLD v1.1 section 7.2 row and names the requirements each pair verifies.

Requirement binding: FGM-01 -> FR-131 (marking bound to every stored partition), FR-135 (purpose, owner, retention rule declared); FGM-02 -> NFR-025 (configured deadline and payload limit terminate fail-safe with audit), NFR-033 (item quota refused before persistence); FGM-03 -> FR-053 (derived memory stays non-canonical memory, no write around the consolidation service); FGM-04 -> FR-115 (cross-run access only through the authorized, correlated service); FGM-05 -> FR-119 (explicit cross-project/federated Authority, zero leakage, cross-tenant deny); FGM-06 -> NFR-075 (versioned workload manifest of every retrieval run); FGM-07 -> FR-131 (embedding descriptors carry marking and purpose, no cross-marking rebuild); FGM-08 -> FR-113 (memory content grants no Authority, never instruction-eligible); FGM-09 -> FR-053 (correction is a new provenanced version, exact replay); FGM-10 -> FR-119, FR-135 (exclusion from result/rank/count/cache/explanation, projections purged). The binding equals exactly the nine requirements whose verification_task is OCOR-DEV-0061 in OCOR_TRACEABILITY_PLAN.csv; BR-003 is not used as a result.

Every FGM case runs the unchanged sealed G5 composition over the real backends via the imported G5 world fixtures (the 0055 world for admission/embedding/retrieval/lifecycle, the 0054 world for consolidation, the 0057 assembler with a PostgreSQL receipt store, the 0059 quota writer with PostgreSQL serialization); a later run is new adapter instances and connections over the same stores and ledger.

Two structural cases (not counted as FGM results) parse the LLD v1.1 section 7.2 table and the traceability plan so that the campaign table, the requirement set and the one-positive/one-negative-per-FGM shape cannot drift silently.

normative_interpretations: Per-requirement evidence location: OCOR_TRACEABILITY_PLAN.csv names reports/evidence/G6/<REQ>.json + raw-log hash as expected_evidence, while the backlog evidence_outputs of OCOR-DEV-0061 and the fail-closed scope gate (scripts/validate_ocor_change_scope.py) admit only reports/evidence/G6/OCOR-DEV-0061.json/.log and the G6 MANIFEST.json. Ambiguity without semantic impact (same tests, backends and raw log): resolved by the most restrictive reading (no write outside the authorized scope), following the sealed G5 practice: one requirement_results entry per (FGM, requirement) inside the task record and in the G6 manifest, each with its positive and negative test, backend, counts and the raw-output sha256. Recorded in the iteration log; no per-requirement file is created.

The backlog validation command 'uv run pytest -q ocor-runtime/tests/conformance/fgm/test_fgm_01_10.py' cannot spawn pytest from the repository root (the root pyproject is a tool configuration without the runtime environment), as for the sealed G5 records; it is executed scoped to the runtime project ('uv run --project ocor-runtime --frozen --extra test --extra lint pytest ...'), same module and arguments.

FGM-06 'equivalenza' is read as: every mode returns only policy-filtered items of the authorized set and pins its representation versions and ranking profile; identical requests over a later run reproduce identical answers. It does not claim that ranking orders coincide across modes (they rank by different representations by design, ADD v1.3 Part II section 2.7).

NFR-075 is verified at the level available to a conformance campaign: the versioned workload manifest of each retrieval run (corpus digests, mode, query digest and contract, representation versions, ranking profile, top_k, backend images) is reproducible and changes with every workload dimension. No benchmark or performance claim is made.

residual_risks: Policy, Authority, stop-epoch, legal-hold and audit decisions in the qualifying cases are the explicit G5 test ports on the real stores; no production authority service is exercised (open, unassigned).
The campaign covers FGM-01..FGM-10 only; FGM-11..FGM-20 belong to OCOR-DEV-0062; full-memory runtime stays NO-GO until the governed closure of FGM-01..FGM-20.

Cross-run persistence is exercised with new adapter instances and connections over the same stores and in-process ledger; a process restart with the journal ledger is covered by the sealed G5 cases, not repeated here.

implementers: Claude Code (Anthropic), claude-opus-5-5, CLI 2.1.310, implementer of record under LOOP-IMPLEMENTER-ORDER-AUTH-FALLBACK (2026-10-26): pre-code inventory, campaign module, qualification and this candidate. No other agent touched OCOR-DEV-0061.
roles.independence: external loop only; the implementer does not verify. Eligible verifier: a provider different from Anthropic and from OpenAI (the loop always counts Codex), i.e. Cursor/Grok (xAI) or Antigravity/Gemini (Google).

rollback_procedure_verified: Mechanical review: the task adds one test module and its evidence (plus the new G6 manifest); no runtime code, schema, migration or existing test changes; rollback is a revert commit of the task merge, after which the G5 manifests and records remain valid unchanged.
